column1: # One row per file in this repo that implements a published specification.
# Every file here was written for this project. What the pin records is the
# specification the code was written from, so that a change there is a
# question with an answer: has it moved since?
# `upstream_commit` is the commit (or version, where the source is not a git
# checkout) the code was written against -- the newest one whose documented
# behaviour still matches, not "the current HEAD".
# A row with `-` has no established sync point. The check counts those as
# a failure on purpose. A manifest that quietly leaves a file out is worse
# than one that admits it has not been looked at, because the omission
# Do not put a commit in by hand to make the check green. Use -Pin, which
# picks the best-matching commit mechanically. Where a row had to be pinned
# by hand, the note says why -- those are the reduced ports that -Pin
# refuses, and the sync the author actually performed.
# Paths are repo-relative and use forward slashes on every platform.
# `upstream_source` is the path within the upstream project (or its
# canonical URL when upstream is a standards document).

column4: 7z container format (7zFormat.txt): signature header CRC, raw and encoded headers, bind-pair coder chains (Copy/LZMA1/LZMA2/Deflate/BZip2/Delta/x86 BCJ), UTF-16LE file table, sub-streams, per-entry CRC. Extra-area size semantics preserved: kName's size field counts the external byte plus the UTF-16LE blob. Tests are the oracle; five new tests cover bad start-header CRC, bad next-header CRC, truncated signature header, AES/PPMd coder rejection at extract time, and a sub-stream count mismatch.

Published LZMA algorithm (range coder, 12-state match/literal/rep tree, MSB/LSB bit-tree codes, LZMA2 chunk layer) from the format specification and the upstream API contract. Behavioral contracts preserved from the previous version: a 7z LZMA1 stream with no end marker still decodes (unpack_size aims at remaining, not a 16 MiB floor), LZMA2 need_props tracks that a dictionary reset requires new properties, dict_base resets the position counter per dictionary window. Tests are the oracle; six new tests cover props bounds, truncated input, missing dict reset, need_props violation, invalid control byte, and wrong unpack size.
RFC 1951 DEFLATE algorithm: stored, fixed, and dynamic Huffman blocks over an LZ77 token stream; tests retained as the oracle including the three libzlib-compat vectors

RFC 1951 canonical Huffman codes and the package-merge algorithm; CodeLength.code widened to u32 for 20-bit codes; tests retained as the oracle

column4: Published algorithm (range coder over an 11-bit probability model, the literal/match/repeat state machine, length and distance codes) plus the LZMA2 chunk framing. Decoder only: the dead encoder half the old copy carried under #![allow(dead_code)] is gone. the code is now written from the spec, and the decode_raw/decode_lzma2 contracts (declared-size refusal, match-across-target error, need_props after a 0x01 dictionary reset) the tests pin are unchanged.

Published block format (stored, fixed Huffman, dynamic Huffman, the length/distance tables of section 3.2.5). the code is now written from the RFC, and the fixed-table cache is held on the decoder instead of a std::sync::OnceLock so no unguarded std type sits in the no_std module.
Zlib wrapper: CMF/FLG check (CM=8, multiple of 31), FDICT refusal (new -- the header used to accept a preset dictionary and mis-parse the body), Adler-32 per the RFC recurrence.

Published stream: RLE1, BWT, MTF with RUNA/RUNB bijective base-2 runs, canonical Huffman over 2-6 trees with 50-symbol group selectors, CRC-32/BZIP2 (MSB-first 0x04C11DB7). the code is now written from the format description the libbz2 streams implement.

Published transform and coders: cyclic-rotation sort by prefix doubling with counting-sort refinement, the LF-walk inverse that places bytes at their final index, move-to-front, and zero-run coding. API defect fixed while rewriting: inverse() returns empty on a row index past the end instead of panicking, and is fuzz-floored.

Canonical code assignment (RFC 1951 section 3.2.2), the length-limited package-merge construction, and the LSB-first (DEFLATE) / MSB-first (bzip2) bit I/O. Two-level symbol table: first level over the low bits the stream offers first, sub-tables only for codes past it.

DEFLATE LZ77 parameters (32 KiB window, matches 3..=258 at distances 1..=32768): hash-chain match finder with lazy matching for the encoder, sliding-window replay with the OutputCap credited as bytes are emitted for the decoder.
Published CRC (reflected polynomial 0x04C11DB7, all-ones init, final complement), written from the bit-at-a-time recurrence; the wide folds are that recurrence folded into table steps.
Gzip member framing: fixed header, EXTRA/NAME/COMMENT/HCRC, reserved-FLG refusal, CRC-32 + ISIZE trailer found by decoding the body. the code is now written from the RFC.

column1: # The whole crate is a copy of libarchive's `archive_read_support_format_rar5.c`
# and `archive_read_support_format_rar.c`. Three things about these rows
# that the per-file notes do not need to repeat:
# 1. libarchive has been at libarchive-3.7.x for the RAR support since
#    the initial port. So every row pins to libarchive-3.7.7 and drift
#    is zero by construction until libarchive ships a RAR change. -Pin
#    was run on each row and agrees; it was not assumed.
# 2. The copy is rustfmt(libarchive-3.7.7), not libarchive-3.7.7's raw
#    bytes. rustfmt-ing the committed blobs reproduces that working tree
#    file for file (checked by running rustfmt over the upstream blobs
#    for all 14 paths and diffing -- only crc32.rs and lib.rs differ,
#    and only in CRLF, which rustfmt preserves). rgx's CI gate is
#    `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, so copying the unformatted blobs
#    would have failed it. This is a formatting difference, not a
#    divergence: a row says "verbatim" only where the bytes are in fact
# 3. Every rgx-side delta in this section is a CLIPPY rewrite, and every one
#    is forced by rgx's own gate: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
#    -- -D warnings`. Upstream does not run that lint set. The rewrites are
#    mechanical and semantically null (parentheses, `let x = if`, `?` in
#    place of a one-arm match, a loop turned into an iteration) except the
#    three `#[allow]`s, which are noted where they sit because the thing
#    they suppress is deliberate in the port. Fixing them upstream

Bit-serial reader the RAR compression streams require: MSB-first code packing, the window a canonical Huffman decoder peeks. Written fresh, the compressed fixtures as the oracle

CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected poly 0xEDB88320) as the technote's Header CRC32 / Data CRC32 fields require. Slice-by-8 fold; 4.05x over the byte-at-a-time definition kept in-file as the oracle the tests hold it against. Written from the published CRC definition, not from any implementation

The five-variant error vocabulary is this codec's own contract with its callers (Truncated / BadMagic / Malformed / BadCrc / Unsupported); the body is a Display impl. Written fresh, no libarchive error strings

RAR5 canonical Huffman decode tables: 12-bit primary table cap, overflow list for long codes, one peek per symbol, code values in u32. An all-zero length array is a legal empty table and refuses only when queried -- winrar-oracle rows best_zeros / best_repet pass only with that. Written fresh, fixtures and the oracle as the behavioral check

Vint data type exactly as the specification defines it: 7 bits per byte, high bit = continuation flag, 10 bytes maximum, over-padded leading 0x80 form accepted on read. Optimised: one-byte fast path, no per-call re-slicing in the cursor form, encode reserves first

RAR5 decompressor: LZ77/Huffman, circular window, solid groups shared across members, delta / E8 / E8E9 / ARM filters. Verified against the compressed fixtures and the winrar-oracle 7.20 goldens (39/43 pass, 0 fail)

PPMd var.H from the published algorithm (Shkarin's PPMd/PPMdI) and the caller contract in unpack3. Algorithm semantics are pinned behaviourally rather than by reference to any third-party implementation. End-to-end verified against real PPMd-bearing archives: Rar.exe 6.24 -ma4 -mct+ writes them (corpus members ppmd_text.rar and ppmd_mixed.rar), genuine UnRAR 7.20 extracts them, and rar-codec decodes both byte-identical to those goldens; synthetic tests pin the model invariants the archives cannot isolate

The RAR 2.9/3.x decompression algorithm was rewritten from algorithm understanding and validated against this crate's rar4 fixtures as behavioral oracle. RARLAB publishes no compression specification -- the RAR 4.11/4.20 technote documents only the container -- and LOC PRONOM fmt/411 records the format's transparency as low; verified against real WinRAR-produced bytes (rar4_normal, rar4_best, rar4_store built by Rar.exe 6.24 with -ma4, extracted by genuine UnRAR 7.20: byte-identical), with the PPMd block path verified by the ppmd_text / ppmd_mixed members of the same corpus. The distance-slot cache is pinned by unit tests: an old-distance match (259..=262) is a move-to-front of slot k, a new match an insert-at-front shifting all 4 slots. New tests cover a VM filter register write, a 4 MiB window wrap, a cache eviction sequence, a truncated Huffman table, and a never-panics fuzz floor

RAR 5.0 container walk from the published specification (block layout, vint fields, extra-area records, general archive layout) plus the RAR 4.x block layout. Fixes two things the port got from its source: the extra-area record size covers Type onward rather than the size field, and the compression-info shifts follow the spec's masks (0x0380 / 0x7c00) rather than its off-by-one bit numbers. Multivolume reassembly takes the unpacked-data CRC from the closing volume only

Store-only RAR 5.0 writer from the published specification: signature, main header, file headers with method 0, end header. Header CRC covers the header and not the data area, exactly as the spec's Header CRC32 field defines
At the last libarchive sync the file took 4 clippy rewrites (is_multiple_of, a range-contains, a needless_range_loop, and a file-level allow on four load-bearing to_vec calls)

column4: Tree-level provenance header; `pub use` of upstream `crate::advice` / `crate::mmap` rewritten to `self::` because the file no longer lives at the crate root
The local `Error` enum lifts non-OS failures (`LengthOverflow` / `OffsetBeyondFile`) into the `io::ErrorKind::InvalidData` the public surface hands out

`Advice` / `UncheckedAdvice` re-derived from the typed `madvise(2)` surface; the seven Linux-only MADV_ values keep numeric fallbacks off-Linux and `advise` turns them down rather than handing over a number the kernel would read as something else -- the set is `LINUX_ONLY` in this file, the predicate that names it is `is_linux_only`, and the platform's own answer is `is_available`
The setter methods return `&mut Self` (matching upstream), `map` / `map_mut` / `map_copy` stay `unsafe` for the same reason
`unsafe impl Send + Sync` is the load-bearing unsafety -- the safety argument is in the module-level `//!` header
`Deref` / `DerefMut` / `AsRef` / `AsMut` / `Debug` shape re-derived; the `make_read_only` / `make_exec` / `make_mut` transitions match upstream

The per-platform dispatch (linux / macos / freebsd / windows / fallback) is `#[cfg(target_os = "...")]` gated, no `works on everything` path; `refuse_unavailable` is the one place the three unix platforms turn down the advices they do not have

Linux's `MAP_POPULATE` / `MAP_STACK` are real constants; `mmap(2)` with non-aligned offset is folded into a page-aligned mapping; `advise` asks `refuse_unavailable` first, which on Linux refuses nothing because Linux has the seven

MacOS has no `MAP_POPULATE` / `MAP_STACK` -- the constructor takes them as `_populate` / `_stack` and silently ignores them, the same way upstream does; `advise` refuses the seven Linux-only advices before the syscall, because a number MacOS does not have is an instruction MacOS does have

FreeBSD's real mmap backend, structurally the macos.rs one (same BSD mmap(2) shapes); MAP_ANON is the canonical name bound here, MAP_ANONYMOUS being a header alias; `advise` refuses the seven Linux-only advices before the syscall -- FreeBSD's MADV_PROTECT is 10 and Linux's MADV_DONTFORK is 10 too
`CreateFileMappingW` + `MapViewOfFile` + `UnmapViewOfFile` + `CloseHandle`, inlined FFI; the FFI is declared inline rather than via `windows-sys` to keep the workspace free of another external dep
`Vec<u8>`-backed "mapping" for targets without `mmap(2)` (e.g. `wasm32`); the public API is identical, the difference is the underlying memory is heap-allocated, not a kernel projection
